text:
sean_sales: Hey team — Acme POC hitting a wall. They set up Redwood SDK and logs show tokens fine but Cloud Logging sink has no spans and trace IDs don't match what our console shows. Can someone help with export/settings?

maria_se: @sean_sales can you paste the example log + the trace header coming from their app? quick check: are they using X-Cloud-Trace-Context or traceparent?

sean_sales: here's a sample from client: 
```json
{"message":"request complete","level":"info","trace":"projects/acme-prod/traces/0004b2f1a"}
```
and the HTTP header they forwarded: `traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01`

tariq_eng: Hmm. That trace id in the JSON is prefixed with `projects/.../traces/`. Stackdriver expects the numeric trace id without the project prefix in some exporters. If they're also sending W3C traceparent we need to ensure our ingest maps it to Cloud Trace format. Are they going through our private deployment or hosted?

sean_sales: Hosted API (dev account). They said "we see traces in their side but not in the Redwood Console -> Traces view".

alex_sre: Two quick things: 1) Check the logging export sink config in GCP console: https://console.cloud.google.com/logs -> Exports. If the sink filters exclude trace logs you won't see spans. 2) Our ingestion adds a `redwood.trace_id` field when it sees W3C header; confirm both our collector and their SDK aren't double-wrapping.

maria_se: Also confirm sampling. If their sampling rate is low, only some spans will appear and it looks like missing traces. Ask them to set sdk sampling to 100% for the POC.

sean_sales: Asked them to flip sampling. They returned a new log sample: 
```json
{"message":"call finished","level":"info","redwood":{"trace_id":"4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736"},"span_id":"00f067aa0ba902b7"}
```

tariq_eng: That looks better. Now check the exporter config in their OTLP/Stackdriver exporter. Common mistake: using the Stackdriver Logging API for logs but forgetting to set the trace field mapping. For otel-collector, need something like: 
```yaml
exporters:
  googlecloud:
    project: "acme-prod"
    use_insecure: false
processors:
  batch:
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [googlecloud]
```
If they use a custom log to metric or sink filter it can strip the trace context.

ingest-bot: deploy log-forwarder v2.3.1 -> noticed 429s to cloud-logging from acme-prod between 10:12–10:17 UTC, throttling set to 50req/s.

alex_sre: 429s explain missing spans — Cloud Logging dropping export, and retried logs may lose trace headers. For POC, either increase sink throughput or enable batching and retry on client side. Our docs have a snippet for batching: `max_export_batch_size: 512` `export_timeout: 30s`.

maria_se: @sean_sales also check IAM on their sink account. If the service account used by the exporter lacks `roles/logging.logWriter` or `roles/cloudtrace.agent`, logs/traces won't be accepted.

sean_sales: Good catch — they used a user token instead of the service account. Asking them to swap now. Quick Q on console: is there a way to correlate a request ID from Redwood logs to GCP trace id automatically? The customer wants a single view in their Splunk as well.

tariq_eng: We surface `x-request-id` and `redwood.trace_id` in our structured logs. Recommend they forward both to Splunk as fields and set a correlation key. For GCP, Cloud Trace expects trace IDs in the format `projects/PROJECT_ID/traces/TRACE_ID` when using the Logging API. If they want Splunk correlation too, keep `x-request-id` unchanged and set it as an additional field.

maria_se: If they need a dashboard, point them at Redwood Console > Observability > Dashboards -> Create new -> datasource: Stackdriver + Logs. There's a quick template for latency + error rate. I can DM the JSON.

sean_sales: They swapped to service account and bumped the batch sizes. New logs show no 429s. Sample now: 
```json
{"message":"response","level":"info","x-request-id":"rq_1234","redwood":{"trace_id":"4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736"},"span_id":"00f067aa0ba902b7"}
```

alex_sre: Great. One more check: ensure the exporter sets `trace` attribute on the Cloud Logging entry. For some SDKs you need to set: `entry.trace = "projects/acme-prod/traces/" + traceId`. If you don't do that, Cloud Trace UI won't show the log-to-trace linkage.

sean_sales: Confirmed. They added `entry.trace` mapping and spans appeared in Redwood Console->Traces. Customer happy, wants this baked into our POC checklist.

maria_se: I'll add a short checklist: sampling=100% (POC), service account roles, batch size >=256, map trace header -> entry.trace, expose x-request-id, watch for 429s.

tariq_eng: I can PR a small doc snippet and an otel-collector example for our sales playbook.

sean_sales: Awesome — thanks everyone :raised_hands: 

ops-bot: Incident note created: "POC acme-prod — logging export misconfig + 429 throttling" assigned to eng-ml for follow-up

sean_sales: marking resolved on my side. will follow up with customer and loop in PR when ready.
